account: Coop Szeged Zrt. and Laurel Kft. opened the 247 Shop on Szent István tér in Szeged at the end of May 2025. It is staffed by day, automated and unstaffed outside normal hours. Cameras running the French company Veesion's software analyze shoppers' movements without identifying faces. They alert a remote dispatch service to gestures such as concealing goods. On 8 October 2025 the Szeged daily Délmagyar reported that a security guard had been placed in the store after closing because of thefts. Thieves had followed customers in and out after the customers opened the door with the app. A thief known to police came in at least twice and was caught quickly with camera footage. The operators said that the guard was temporary while the system was fine-tuned, and that the rate of abuse was no higher than in traditional shops. On 9 October 2025 the operators issued a press release, relayed by Index.hu and MTI. It said that over four and a half months the system had exposed three theft attempts. In one, a person hid products under their clothing during night mode. Police caught the perpetrator within hours using the footage. Dates, recovered goods and any police statement are not reported. The operators also said that 8,500 people had shopped in the automated night system in four and a half months, and that shrinkage had not risen despite the longer opening hours. On 30 September 2026 the two companies opened a second store that is unstaffed after hours, a full supermarket on Temesvári körút, after more than 27,000 unstaffed purchases in a year at the first store. The report on the opening describes camera monitoring and a remote dispatch service and does not name Veesion.

ai_role.statement: By the operators' account, the Veesion software flagged the concealment and alerted the remote dispatcher, and the operator then filed a police report. Police caught the perpetrator from the footage within hours. Délmagyar's account of the thief that it reports credits the camera footage and does not mention an alert. It also reports that thieves entered and left behind customers who had opened the door with the app. The operators said that the system was being fine-tuned after these cases, with a security guard in the store for a few days. No source separates what the alert added from what recorded footage alone would have given police.

fields.account: Coop Szeged Zrt. and Laurel Kft. opened the 247 Shop on Szent István tér in Szeged at the end of May 2025. It is staffed by day, automated and unstaffed outside normal hours. Cameras running the French company Veesion's software analyze shoppers' movements without identifying faces. They alert a remote dispatch service to gestures such as concealing goods. On 8 October 2025 the Szeged daily Délmagyar reported that a security guard had been placed in the store after closing because of thefts. Thieves had followed customers in and out after the customers opened the door with the app. A thief known to police came in at least twice and was caught quickly with camera footage. The operators said that the guard was temporary while the system was fine-tuned, and that the rate of abuse was no higher than in traditional shops. On 9 October 2025 the operators issued a press release, relayed by Index.hu and MTI. It said that over four and a half months the system had exposed three theft attempts. In one, a person hid products under their clothing during night mode. Police caught the perpetrator within hours using the footage. Dates, recovered goods and any police statement are not reported. The operators also said that 8,500 people had shopped in the automated night system in four and a half months, and that shrinkage had not risen despite the longer opening hours. On 30 September 2026 the two companies opened a second store that is unstaffed after hours, a full supermarket on Temesvári körút, after more than 27,000 unstaffed purchases in a year at the first store. The report on the opening describes camera monitoring and a remote dispatch service and does not name Veesion.
